a message spanning three or more blocks would exercise chaining across a longer sequence.","fix":"Add one longer message whose padding spans three blocks and chain through it."}],"strengths":["The oracle is external: every expected digest is a published FIPS 180-4 value, so neither the testbench nor the design defines correctness, and a self-consistent but wrong implementation cannot pass.","The two-block vector exercises chaining end to end, and the init-high negative case proves the chaining path is genuinely selected rather than incidentally matching.","done is caught on its rising edge with a shadow of the DUT's own strobe, never a reference-model signal, so a stuck or repeated strobe cannot desynchronise the suite.","Stimulus is applied only in the settled region after step(), including the reset windows, so no input is sampled at an extra edge.","The block-capture test actively corrupts block_in every cycle after the start edge, which turns an implicit assumption into a measured property.","Every Must requirement has its own task with a covers annotation, and the main block calls all fifteen tasks before the summary.","The wait loops now report guard expiry as its own failure, so a hung core is distinguishable from a wrong digest.","Each block literal is documented as the padding of its named message, so a reader can re-derive it without recomputation."],"summary":"The suite covers all eleven Must requirements and all four Should requirements against five independently published digests, which is the strongest oracle available for a hash core: neither the design nor the testbench defines correctness. The sequential behaviours are measured rather than assumed — repeated starts ignored, back-to-back chaining on the done cycle, one-cycle done, busy held throughout, block latched at start, reset abandoning work in flight — and a hung core now reports as a hang rather than as a mismatch. The one remaining gap is breadth beyond two-block messages."}
